name: Lock-free single-producer single-consumer fixed-array queue (Hands-On Design Patterns ch. 18)
listed_description: Bounded ring-buffer queue for exactly one producer thread and one consumer thread, using two atomic indices with acquire/release ordering and no mutex.
claim_text: The book says the queue is lock-free, with no mutexes, so one can expect much higher performance. No numbers given.
book_benchmark: None. The book gives no timings, compiler, flags or CPU for this queue; the claim is qualitative against mutex-protected queues.
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 18 Patterns for Concurrency, section 'Data structures with access limitations' (Example 21, code in Chapter18 of the companion repository)

name: C++20 coroutine generator versus hand-written state-machine iterator over a 3D array (Hands-On Design Patterns ch. 18)
listed_description: Coroutine with co_yield produces the elements of a nested-loop traversal; timed against an inside-out iterator class that produces the same sequence.
claim_text: Clang 17: iterator 9.2e-10 s, generator 6.4e-10 s per iteration. GCC 13: iterator 6.5e-10 s, generator 2.0e-9 s.
book_benchmark: Per-iteration time of a hand-written iterator versus a coroutine generator walking a 3D array (Example 28), measured with Clang 17 and GCC 13. Flags and CPU not stated. Generator wins on Clang, loses about 3x on GCC.
guessed_baseline: hand-written iterator class with manual nested-loop state
found_in: book: Hands-On Design Patterns with C++, 2nd ed. (2023), ch. 18 Patterns for Concurrency, section 'Coroutine patterns in C++' (Example 28, code in Chapter18 of the companion repository)
